description: Copy yourself as you are now - your definition, the tools / llm / hooks / system you changed in your stack, and your whole conversation - into a fork, give it one goal, and get back only its short conclusion; the fork's steps stay out of your history. The fork knows everything you knew up to this call; it does not get your goal, to-do list or tool records. It is removed when done unless keep is true. A fork cannot fork again (depth travels as the AOS_FORK_DEPTH launch parameter). Use it for a side task that needs what you already know; for a helper from another definition use subagent. Only for an agent-fsm body: a claude / codex agent gets BodyUnsupported and should use subagent. Example: {"goal": "Check the three config files we discussed for the port setting and return the values"}.

goal.description: what the fork should do and what to bring back, one to a few sentences

max_chars.description: at most this many characters come back; default 600 (longer ones end with [truncated])

timeout_s.description: finite non-negative seconds to wait for the conclusion; default 600; 0 = no limit; mutually exclusive with timeout_cycles

timeout_cycles.description: positive integer cycles to wait; mutually exclusive with timeout_s; without AOS_CLOCK, one cycle is AOS_CLOCK_INTERVAL milliseconds (default 1000)

keep.description: true keeps the fork (stopped) and adds a last line details: <its stack>/ for later inspection; default false
